venue.name: Comox Air Force Museum
venue.description: The Comox Air Force Museum sits at the main entrance to 19 Wing Comox, on the corner of Ryan Road and Military Row. Its galleries run from the First World War through the Second World War, Korea, the Cold War and UN peacekeeping to Afghanistan, and include a CF-101 Voodoo ejection seat, a hands on air traffic control display, a replica Great Escape tunnel and activity books for children. A short distance away on Military Row, the Heritage Air Park holds full size aircraft that have flown at 19 Wing, out in the open where you can walk right up to them. Admission is by donation.
venue.address: 19 Wing Comox, PO Box 1000 Stn. Forces, Lazo, BC V0R 2K0

facility_notes.bus_parking: We have a small parking lot in front of the museum. Additional parking for RVs, trucks and overflow is available across the street at the Canex. Please do not park on the grass verge. Parking is available at the entrance to the Heritage Air Park.

restrictions: Please do not park on the grass verge.
venue.hours_notes: Museum and Heritage Air Park, Tuesday to Sunday, 10am to 4pm. Admission is by donation.

programs.name: Tours and Educational Programming
programs.description: The museum advertises guided tours and educational programmes about the history of the RCAF and the aircraft flown at 19 Wing Comox, with a link that opens an email to the museum to book. They do not publish who it is for, how long it runs, how many can come or what it costs.
programs.our_note: There is a real programme here, but almost nothing published about it. Email the museum and ask about ages, length and group size before you build a morning around it, because the page is a paragraph of description and a booking link and nothing else.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms, an indoor place to eat and any rain cover are not mentioned anywhere on the site, and the museum's own car park is described as small. One call would settle all of it at once.
programs.extra_fees_note: Admission to the museum is by donation. No separate charge for a tour is published.
programs.evidence: Embark on an immersive journey through the fascinating history of the RCAF with our engaging educational programs and tours.

programs.name: Self-guided museum and Heritage Air Park visit
programs.description: The museum's self guided route starts at the dawn of military aviation in the First World War, loops through the Second World War, Korea, the Cold War and UN peacekeeping, then a squadron section, and ends at Afghanistan and post 9/11. Along the way are a CF-101 Voodoo ejection seat, a hands on air traffic control centre, an Argus 18 cylinder engine and a viewing lounge showing short films, plus activity books for children and youth. The Heritage Air Park a short distance along Military Row holds aircraft that have flown at 19 Wing, along with the Heritage Stones, the search and rescue memorial and the Clarkston Memorial. Admission is by donation.
programs.what_children_do: Follow the gallery loop at their own pace, try the CF-101 Voodoo ejection seat and the hands on air traffic control display, sit in the viewing lounge for a short film and work through an activity book. Outside at the air park they can walk right up to parked aircraft and around the memorials.
programs.our_note: This is the side of the museum with things children can put their hands on, and the air park is a reasonable place to eat outside on a dry day. Nothing is published about washrooms or anywhere indoors to sit and eat, so ask when you call. The air park is a separate stop a few hundred metres away, not part of the same building.
programs.practical_summary: There is a small car park at the museum with more space across the road at the Canex, and the air park has parking at its entrance. Washrooms, an indoor lunch spot and rain cover are not mentioned at all, so those are worth a call before you go.
programs.evidence: Try out our CF-101 Voodoo ejection seat and hands-on Air Traffic Control centre.

images.alt: An indoor museum gallery with a large white missile on a yellow wheeled stand in the middle of the floor, a red and white torpedo shaped object hanging from the ceiling, and wall panels of aircraft photographs and text.
A yellow and red twin rotor search and rescue helicopter parked on grass under a blue sky, with a small olive green military jeep on the grass in front of it.
A museum display of military uniforms on mannequins, with leather flying gear, bags and boots arranged on the floor in front, against a wall of enlarged black and white photographs.
A grey fighter jet marked 030 parked on grass in front of a low blue and grey building, with a chain link fence and a car park visible behind it.

gaps: The tours and educational programming are advertised in one paragraph with a booking link and nothing else. No ages, no group size, no length, no price and no notice period. Everything about that programme has to come from an email or a phone call.

The site never uses the word school, class or daycare anywhere. We have recorded that they host school groups on the strength of a bookable educational programme, not on their own wording. Whether a group of children under five is welcome is not stated at all.
Washrooms are not mentioned anywhere on the site.
There is no indoor lunch space mentioned. The air park page invites you to bring a picnic, but no tables, shelter or seating are described, so an indoor fallback in the rain is unknown.

Nothing is said about wheelchair access, stroller access, or whether a bus can park. The museum's own car park is described as small, with overflow for RVs and trucks across the street at the Canex. Buses are not mentioned either way.
Admission is by donation, so there is no fixed price to record for either programme and neither one clears the app's cost bar. That is the honest state, not a missing lookup.

The only address published is a mailing one, a PO box at 19 Wing Comox. They describe the museum itself as being at the main entrance to 19 Wing on the corner of Ryan Road and Military Row, and the Heritage Air Park as a few hundred metres away on Military Row / Little River Road. The coordinates come from the Google Maps place pin on their contact page, which carries the !8m2!3d!4d place marker rather than only a map centre.

STALENESS FLAG. The gallery page says the special exhibits gallery is 'currently showcasing' the RCAF 1924 to 2024 centenary exhibit, and the main navigation still leads with an RCAF 2024 item. What is actually on now may have changed.
The heritage air park page was last touched a long time before the rest of the site, so its detail may be older than the events page.

Alt text for all four images was written after opening each image URL in a browser and looking at the picture. Three of the four are CSS background images on the home page and do not appear to a plain image scan of the markup.
The site offers an English and French language switcher, but that is the website being translated. Nothing says tours are given in French, so no tour languages have been recorded.

conflicts.note: A banner across the top of every page says the museum is open Tuesday to Sunday, 10am to 4pm. A pop up on those same pages says it is closed to the public until April 3rd, with no year given. Phone before you travel.

conflicts.note: Two of their pages give different distances between the museum and the air park, 500 metres on one and 600 metres on the other. Either way the aircraft are a separate stop along Military Row, not beside the building, so plan for a short move between the two.
